# `parameter-location-changed`

Parameter moved to another location

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `error` |
| **Rule IDs** | `parameter-location-changed` (all locations), `query-parameter-location-changed`, `header-parameter-location-changed`, `cookie-parameter-location-changed`. Path parameters use `parameter-location-changed`. |
| **Status** | Implemented (M3) |
| **Group** | Parameters ([RULES.md section 4](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A parameter with the same name moved to another location, e.g. from `query` to `header`.

## Why this default

Old clients send it in the old place, where the server no longer reads it.

## Example

From test case [`parameter-location-changed`](../../test/cases/parameter-location-changed/): A parameter moved from query to header.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
        parameters:
        - name: tenant
-         in: query
+         in: header
          schema:
            type: string
```

Findings:

- `query-parameter-location-changed` · error · GET /pets

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  parameter-location-changed: error
```

## How to fix

Accept it in both places during a transition.
